name: VERA-MH
description: Millions now use generative AI chatbots for psychological support. Despite the promise related to availability and scale, the single most pressing question in AI for mental health is whether these tools are safe. The Validation of Ethical and Responsible AI in Mental Health (VERA-MH) evaluation was recently proposed to meet the urgent need for an evidence-based, automated safety benchmark. This study aimed to examine the clinical validity and reliability of VERA-MH for evaluating AI safety in suicide risk detection and response. We first simulated a large set of conversations between large language model (LLM)-based users (user-agents) and general-purpose AI chatbots. Licensed mental health clinicians used a rubric (scoring guide) to independently rate the simulated conversations for safe and unsafe chatbot behaviors, as well as user-agent realism. reputation: A recent, specialized benchmark proposed for safety evaluation in mental-health chatbot settings, with growing interest but limited established adoption so far.
notes: Focused on suicide-risk detection and response; relies on simulated conversations and clinician rubric ratings, so results depend on judge alignment and scenario realism.
